title: Inbound usage adapter and gated schema registry
creator: Asha Kapoor
description:
Problem: The Console telemetry pipeline currently accepts heterogeneous usage events from multiple producers (UI, SDKs, backend jobs). Producers have different event shapes and we surface intermittent errors and metric regressions when invalid payloads slip through. Existing validators are brittle: tight schema checks cause cascading drops and broad permissive parsing causes downstream enrichment to fail silently.

Goal: Replace the ad-hoc acceptance layer with a pluggable inbound adapter that: 1) performs tenant-aware transformation and validation using a gated schema registry, 2) supports soft-rejection modes for graceful rollout, 3) emits rich telemetry (per-tenant validation rate, rejection reasons, latency) and 4) exposes a simple schema ops API for PMs and integrators to iterate on event contracts.

Scope: Backend services for Console usage event ingestion and the schema validation service. This ticket covers: the adapter service, integration with the schema registry, validation strategies (strict vs. soft-accept), telemetry, CI harness for schema regression tests, and canary rollout automation. Not included: downstream analytics storage optimization and long-term retention policies (follow-up tickets).
acceptance_criteria: Adapter accepts raw events from Kafka topic 'console-usage-inbound' and emits normalized events to 'console-usage-validated'
Per-tenant schema lookup is implemented via the gated registry API with caching TTLs configurable per-tenant
Support two validation modes: 'strict' (reject non-conformant events with detailed reason) and 'soft' (ingest event with 'validation_warnings' metadata). Mode is configurable per-tenant
Expose metrics: validation_rate, rejection_rate, avg_validation_latency, top_rejection_reasons and make them available in Console dashboards
Canary rollout that routes 5% of traffic through strict mode for 48h with automatic rollback on error budget breach
End-to-end test harness that runs schema regression tests for all existing producer contracts and fails PRs on detected breaking changes
Documentation: README and Confluence design doc with schema ops workflow and runbooks for resolving validation failures
Load tested at 12k events/sec with median validation latency < 35ms and p95 < 120ms on dedicated staging cluster
tasks: Design API for pluggable transforms and validation hooks
Implement inbound adapter service (consumer -> transform -> validate -> producer)
Build gated schema registry service with versioning and tenant ACLs
Add caching layer for schemas with metrics and eviction policy
Integrate adapter with existing Kafka topics and consumer groups
Add telemetry hooks and dashboard panels in Console
Create end-to-end regression test suite and CI job
Plan and execute canary rollout with traffic shaping and rollback policy
Author runbooks and Confluence guide for schema owners
notes: Trade-offs: We can do client-side schema enforcement (SDKs) but cannot rely on producers to update; server-side gated registry provides central control and visibility.

Technology choices: initial implementation will use our existing Kafka cluster and a lightweight validation engine based on JSON Schema + custom semantic checks. If CPU becomes a bottleneck, we'll consider migrating validation to a Flink job or native C++ worker pool for hot paths.

Backpressure: adapter will respect consumer group lag and push back producers via topic-level throttles. Short-term we will use broker-side quotas; long-term plan includes token-bucket admission at the API edge.
Soft-rejection mode is critical for onboarding third-party integrations without breaking pipelines; default tenant mode will be 'soft' unless explicitly requested.
Schema ops: schema owners can propose new versions via the schema registry UI; changes must pass compatibility checks in CI before activation. Non-breaking additive changes can auto-promote.
Security: schema registry endpoints require team-scoped tokens and RBAC. We'll add an audit trail for schema publishes and rollbacks.
progress_updates: 2025-02-12: Kickoff meeting with Console, SDK, and Platform teams. Agreed on soft-rejection rollout pattern and telemetry signals.
2025-02-20: Prototype adapter implemented that performs JSON Schema validation against an in-memory registry. Local tests pass for existing producers.
2025-02-28: Benchmarked prototype: CPU bound at ~8k events/sec per 4vCPU worker with current validation library. Need optimization or additional workers for 12k target.
2025-03-05: Decided to add a compiled validation path using rust-validator bindings to reduce latency for high-throughput tenants. Engineering spike approved.
2025-03-10: Schema registry MVP endpoints merged; ACLs and audit log still pending. Starting integration tests with adapter on staging.
2025-03-12: Canary plan drafted: 5% traffic strict mode for 48h, abort if rejection_rate > 1% or validation_latency p95 > 200ms. Tickets opened for monitoring alerts.
